heading: Kota Doria: the airy checked weave of Rajasthan

p: Kota Doria is a handwoven fabric from the Kota region of Rajasthan, made mainly in Kaithoon and the villages around it. Its signature is a pattern of tiny squares called khats, which appear because the weaver groups the warp and weft threads in a fixed rhythm. Hold the fabric up to the light and you will see a fine, see-through grid.

Traditionally it is woven from cotton, often mixed with silk yarn: cotton gives strength and breathability, and silk adds a soft sheen. The name Kota Doria has a Geographical Indication (GI) tag, which protects fabric woven in this region.

The open check weave lets air through, so Kota Doria is one of the lightest fabrics you can wear in Indian summers and humid weather abroad. It is crisp rather than clingy, drapes softly, and takes both dyes and hand block prints well, which is why it is loved for dupattas, kurtas and sarees.

list: Day functions, pujas and festive lunches, when you want to look dressed up but stay cool.
Office wear in summer, with a lining or slip so the sheer weave stays opaque.
As a dupatta over a plain cotton suit: it adds texture without weight.

sections.h: How to care for Kota Doria
list: Dry clean the first time, or hand wash gently in cold water with a mild detergent.
Do not wring or twist; roll the fabric in a towel to remove water.
Dry in shade and iron on low heat while slightly damp. A light starch brings back the crisp feel.

faq: Is Kota Doria cotton or silk?
It is woven from cotton or from a blend of cotton and silk. The silk blend has a gentle sheen; pure cotton is more matte and even more breathable.
How can I tell real Kota Doria?
Look for the small square checks (khats) formed by the weave itself, not printed on top. Handwoven pieces also show tiny irregularities from the loom.
The weave is sheer, so kurtas are usually lined or worn with a slip. Dupattas are often left unlined to show off the checks.
It can shrink a little in hot water. Wash it in cold water or dry clean it.
